dedupe_keys.name: replication package for the paper modeling insights from the austrian national gas grid under declining natural gas demand and increasing domestic renewable gas generation by 2040

description: Sebastian Zwickl-Bernhard and colleagues publish data and Python code for studying Austria's gas network under decarbonisation scenarios to 2040. A mixed-integer model represents pipeline routes, capacities, ages and network levels, comparing continued operation, replacement and decommissioning against trucking and local storage alternatives. It derives network costs and customer-tariff estimates. The January 2024 Zenodo package is free under CC BY 4.0; the linked Energy Economics Group repository at TU Wien identifies GPL-3.0 for code. The documented result is that distributed renewable-gas production can preserve the need for an extensive network despite lower utilisation. This is conditional on the study scenarios and assumptions, not a measured future outcome. The package supports replication of gas-transition investment simulations, but internal file formats, proprietary source restrictions and solver requirements were not fully established. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this application. The Energy Reports paper is the describing citation.
